- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days; reduce initial values by 5–10% relative to historical mean.
- Underestimate sharp downward spikes (e.g., below 40) — adjust downward by 2–5% to match observed volatility.
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., post-45.0) — cap forecast at 45.0–46.0 for 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >45.0 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence to 40–44.
- Lagged underestimation in late horizon (days 20–30): add 1–3% to forecast to account for delayed rebound.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 5 days are >44.0, reduce forecast by 2–4% to prevent false momentum.
